subject: Specifying model to obtain heterogeneity index

messages.author: b940bb03851c507a
messages.subject: Specifying model to obtain heterogeneity index
parts:
Hi, I'm trying to run an independent pathway model to obtain a heterogeneity index for a hierarchical model.

The model in which SNP operates through the factor was specified as below.

model <- "F1 =~ 1*V8 + V7 + V6 + V3
        F2 =~ 1*V1 + V2 + V6 + V5 + V3
        F3 =~ 1*V4 + V5 + V6
        M =~ 1*F1 + F2 + F3
        V5 ~~ a*V5
        a > 0.001
        M ~ SNP
        "


And below is how I am planning to specify an independent pathway.

model <- "F1 =~ 1*V8 + V7 + V6 + V3
        F2 =~ 1*V1 + V2 + V6 + V5 + V3
        F3 =~ 1*V4 + V5 + V6
        M =~ 1*F1 + F2 + F3
        V5 ~~ a*V5
        a > 0.001
        V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5 + V6 + V7 + V8 ~ SNP
        "

I just want to double-check if this is the correct way to represent the independent pathway for the second-order factor (M) of the hierarchical model. Should the SNP effect be on the first-order factors or the genetic indicators?

Thanks,
Austin

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: Specifying model to obtain heterogeneity index
parts:
Hi Austin,

The independent pathways model can be specified to operate on the first order factors (rather than the higher order factors) or on the individual traits. You should interpret accord to which specification you use. I can imagine wanting to specify on the first order factors (so it's still a common pathways model through those factors but not through the higher order factor), and then from there specifying yet another independent pathways model to operate on the individual traits (or perhaps several, where you free up independent pathways for one first order factor at a time). That way you can get at heterogeneity at each level.

You can read through the 11 disorder paper by Grotzinger et al. in Nature Genetics to see the approach that we specifically took for the hierarchical p factor model.

I can't recall off hand what the defaults are for allowing independent variables to correlate with factors. When you run the model in some tests SNPs with your code you should make sure that the SNP doest covary with the factor(s) by default (you can always fix those covariances to 0 to be sure) in your independent pathways model.

Elliot
